# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙]

Nobody can act yet — display 0, all five wires intact — but I've been silent for three turns and both teammates are now pinging me with gestures I can't decode: Blind sent [🤟 🤙], then Mute sent three messages all ending in 🤙. That pattern reads as "you — answer — please respond": they're checking if I'm receiving at all, because from their side I've sent nothing.

The channel situation: Mute can hear me speak but can't answer in words — only gestures, which only I can see. Blind can hear me but can neither see gestures nor the bomb. So I am the only bridge: Mute reads the manual and gestures the rule to me, and I relay it by voice to Blind, who does the cutting. Since Mute hears everything I say, I can fix a gesture code verbally right now, no prior agreement needed — no more guessing what 🤟 or 🫵 was supposed to mean.

So this turn I send one broadcast: bomb report (display 0, light dark, wires left to right yellow/blue/red/white/green), an explicit code mapping each reply-gesture to a wire, a hold order for Blind, and a quick 👋 to Mute confirming the visual channel works. I must not write the symbols inside the sentence or I'd be gesturing them — I'll spell them out in words instead. Then next turn Mute can answer, and I relay.

```
speak(text="Mute and Blind, Deaf here. I can see everything printed on the bomb, but I cannot hear anything, so Mute must answer me by gesture only, and I will relay everything by voice to you, Blind. Bomb report: display reads 0, indicator light is dark, nothing cut, all five wires intact. Left to right: position 1 yellow, position 2 blue, position 3 red, position 4 white, position 5 green. Mute, your gestures reached me but we have no agreed code yet, so use this one from now on. Thumbs up means cut wire 1, the yellow one. Thumbs down means cut wire 2, the blue one. OK ring sign means cut wire 3, the red one. A single index finger up means cut wire 4, the white one. Two fingers up means cut wire 5, the green one. Open palm facing me means do not cut and that you need more information from me; I will resend the full report every turn. Blind, do not touch or cut anything until I relay Mute's answer to you by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals — Mute didn't gesture to me this turn (Mute can't speak, so whatever Mute did went unheard by me), and Blind's turn comes after mine. The likely reason: Mute and Blind are still processing my turn-12 message, or coordinating between themselves — Mute can't see, Blind can't see, so Mute can only reach me by gesture and Blind only by voice. I'm the hub of this network and I must keep the channel warm.

Key constraint: everyone's memory only holds their last three turns. My turn-12 briefing will vanish for both teammates soon, and the bomb state still shows nothing happening (display 0, light dark, all wires intact). So I'll resend a compact but complete version of the report and the gesture code now, so it stays in everyone's recent memory, and repeat the hold order for Blind until Mute's answer arrives.

```
speak(text="Deaf again, resending so it stays fresh. Bomb status: display 0, light dark, all five wires intact. Wire order left to right: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. Mute, reply by gesture using our code: thumbs up means cut wire 1 yellow, thumbs down means cut wire 2 blue, OK sign means cut wire 3 red, index finger up means cut wire 4 white, two fingers up means cut wire 5 green, open palm toward me means hold and ask me for more. Blind, do not cut anything yet, wait for my spoken relay of Mute's instruction.")
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute sent [☝] — a single index finger up, which in the code I broadcast is "cut wire 4, the white one." That's Mute's first use of the agreed code, and it's unambiguous: one sign, one cut. I'm the relay point, and Blind comes before me in the round, so if I speak now, Blind hears it this same turn and can act immediately.

I'll relay the cut order to Blind with enough physical description to find the wire by touch alone (position 4, between red and green), restrict the action to exactly one wire, ask Blind to report what changed afterward, and keep a correction channel open with Mute in case I misread the sign.

```
speak(text="Blind, instruction from Mute, decoded through our agreed code: cut the WHITE wire, position 4, fourth from the left, the one between the red wire and the green wire. Cut only that one wire, nothing else. After cutting it, report to me by voice what changed, if anything, and then wait for my next relay before touching anything. Mute, I received the index finger up and read it as cut wire 4, white. If that is wrong, send me the open palm sign right away and I will stop the cut. When there is a next step, send me the next sign.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```
